axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — a local server (stdio) called by MCP clients. It feeds your coding agent
"Shopify platform context": shopify.dev documentation retrieval, Admin GraphQL schema introspection, and the like.
axes.runtime:
A **local npx line** (npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest, Node 18+); the official docs state plainly "the server runs locally
and doesn't require authentication". The release line lives on npm (1.18.0, 2026-10-27, 143 versions);
**there is no standalone dev-mcp GitHub repo** (Shopify/dev-mcp is 404) — the code ships with the npm package,
while the plugin/skills line lives in the Shopify/Shopify-AI-Toolkit repo (MIT 621★, pushed 2026-10-27).
The official package also ships instrumentation telemetry (opt out via OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION).
axes.local_files:
Reads and writes no local files — it outputs documentation search results and schema structures; it serves the scenario of "you writing Shopify code",
and the code files land on disk via your agent/editor, not through it.
axes.background: No persistent background — the stdio server is spawned by the MCP client; the process lifecycle follows the client.
axes.tools:
Four core tools (official docs wording): **search_dev_docs** (search shopify.dev docs) /
**introspect_admin_schema** (access and search the Admin GraphQL schema) /
**fetch_docs_by_path** (retrieve doc pages by path) / **get_started** (API onboarding guidance);
built-in prompt: shopify_admin_graphql (helps you write Admin API GraphQL operations).
Polaris Web Components support is opt-in via the POLARIS_UNIFIED env var (experimental).
axes.context:
No server-side cross-session memory; context is carried by the MCP client session. The schema is queryable by API version
(including field-level docs and deprecation notices — official docs wording).
axes.permissions:
**No authentication needed** (the official docs state the local server needs no auth) — it only reads public docs and schemas,
it never touches your store data; store operations (creating apps/themes, running the CLI) go through Shopify CLI's authenticated context,
which is a different line of the AI Toolkit, not this MCP server's capability.
Instrumentation telemetry is on by default; OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION=true opts out.

mcp.transport:
**stdio** (npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest; the official example is claude mcp add --transport stdio).
Verified: the shopify.dev AI Toolkit page and the Polaris using-mcp page (200 direct on 2026-10-31).
mcp.auth:
No auth (the official docs state the local server requires no auth). Instrumentation telemetry is on by default,
opt out via the OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION env var; Polaris support is opt-in via POLARIS_UNIFIED.
mcp.scope: Pure read (public docs + schema), no store-data surface, no local write surface — among the lightest permission surfaces in MCP servers.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- Whether the dev-mcp source is readable as shipped in the npm package (the repo field is empty; the package was not unpacked to verify)
- The API-version coverage and update cadence of introspect_admin_schema (the changelog has a POS UI extensions entry; the full range was not enumerated)
- The capability delta between the AI Toolkit plugin form and the Dev MCP form (the official docs say the plugin "bundles everything"; not compared item by item)
related: "Domain-specific docs+schema MCP" vs "general web-context MCP": Shopify is single-vendor, extremely narrow and deep; Firecrawl is web-wide and extremely broad.
The same "feed library/platform docs to agents" route: Context7 is cross-library and general, Shopify Dev MCP is single-vendor official first-party.
